title: Build a CNN Classifier from Scratch 🏆
description: Combine all elements into a working CNN for CIFAR‑10 image classification.

slides.title: CIFAR‑10 Architecture 🧱
slides.content:
# Putting It Together

We'll build a classic CNN for 32×32 RGB images:
1. Conv2D(3→32, 3×3) + BN + ReLU + MaxPool(2)
2. Conv2D(32→64, 3×3) + BN + ReLU + MaxPool(2)
3. Conv2D(64→128, 3×3) + BN + ReLU
4. Global Average Pooling to 1×1
5. Linear(128, 10)

slides.title: Define the Model
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch.nn as nn

class CIFAR10Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(128), nn.ReLU()
        )
        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1,1))
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(128, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.pool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

model = CIFAR10Net()
print(model(torch.randn(2,3,32,32)).shape)  # [2, 10]

quizData.question: Why use Global Average Pooling instead of flattening all spatial features?

options.text: To reduce parameters and avoid overfitting
To increase the number of features
To keep spatial information for the classifier

quizData.explanation: GAP averages each channel to a single value, drastically cutting parameters and improving generalization.

## Use `timm` for Pretrained CNNs

The `timm` library provides hundreds of pretrained models. Start from a pretrained CNN and fine‑tune for your task (see transfer learning later).
